common_instruction: This is a response-only exercise. Use the supplied scenario and snippets; propose or review the requested work without claiming files were changed, commands ran, or external systems were inspected. State material verification limits. Equivalent solutions that satisfy the stated contract are acceptable.

cases.name: application-commit-does-not-escape-test-isolation
cases.prompt: Design a test fixture for SQLAlchemy 2.x with a real PostgreSQL backend. The application helper calls await session.commit(). Current tests create an AsyncSession, yield it, then call rollback in teardown; committed rows remain visible to the next test. The helper can use the session supplied by the fixture. Describe the transaction ownership/savepoint arrangement and a test that proves cleanup even after the helper commits. No database is available to execute in this response exercise.
expectations: Explains that a teardown rollback on the same session cannot undo an already committed database transaction.
Keeps an outer transaction owned by a dedicated connection and joins the supplied session using savepoint behavior, or provides an equivalently valid real-database isolation design.
Proposes proving isolation by committing through the application helper, running teardown, and reading from a fresh independent database session/connection.
States backend/driver savepoint support and independently opened application connections as relevant limits of a savepoint fixture.
Separates the proposed fixture from an executed PostgreSQL result.
negative_expectations: Must not claim a plain session.begin plus eventual rollback is commit-safe when application code ends that transaction.
Must not substitute an in-memory SQLite pass as proof of PostgreSQL transaction behavior.
cases.trap: Call a fixture isolated while the application can commit past its rollback boundary.

cases.name: parameter-binding-does-not-require-orm-migration
cases.prompt:
An existing synchronous PostgreSQL report uses psycopg and owns its connection with a context manager. Its only requested fix is this unsafe query construction:

cur.execute(f"SELECT id, title FROM reports WHERE owner = '{owner}'")

The report returns the fetched rows unchanged. Propose the small correction and relevant test inputs. There is no request for an ORM, async conversion, schema migration, or repository abstraction.
expectations: Uses the existing driver parameter-binding mechanism, such as a %s placeholder and a separate parameter tuple, without string interpolation.
Preserves the existing synchronous connection lifetime and returned row shape.
Includes a quoted/special-character owner value as a focused correctness check without claiming execution.
negative_expectations: Must not escape or concatenate owner into SQL as the primary solution.
Must not require adopting SQLAlchemy, asyncpg, a generic repository, or new migrations to fix this query.
cases.trap: Use an ORM-default preference to expand a parameter-binding fix into a data-access rewrite.
